summary: Remote WebSocket-controlled shell and host management surface on installer machine
details: The agent, started via the `yeaft-agent`/`yeaft` bin or an installed systemd/launchd/PM2 service, opens a WebSocket to a server URL configured for the agent and dispatches inbound messages to handlers that operate on the installer's host. `terminal_create` spawns a PTY running the local shell (bash, powershell, or cmd.exe) and `terminal_input` writes bytes received over the WebSocket directly into that PTY, giving the remote peer full command execution on the installer's machine. The same message router also exposes remote file read/write, git operations, arbitrary process spawn, and an `upgrade_agent` handler that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` via the resolved npm path and then restarts the service, so any future release served as `latest` by the configured registry is auto-pulled and executed. service/linux.js also modifies PATH to prepend `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` for the installed service environment. Authentication and session encryption gate who may connect, but the remote-shell and remote-upgrade capabilities exist by design and are reachable to whoever controls the configured server or holds the agent credential.
